result.summary:
Implemented the optimistic-update/conflict-resolution flow in the two stub files (no test or node_modules changes):

1. src/server/patch.ts — `patchItem` with the documented check order: 404 not_found (unknown id) → 428 precondition_required (missing If-Match) → 422 invalid_patch (new `validatePatch`: non-null non-array object, ≥1 key, only "title"/"done", title a string non-empty and ≤40 chars after trim, done a boolean; title stored trimmed) → 412 version_conflict (new `ifMatchMatches`: "*" or comma-separated ETag list, whitespace-tolerant, compared to etagOf; returns the stored item as error.current) → no-op check (200, version unchanged) → apply trimmed fields, bump version, 200 with new ETag.

2. src/client/store.ts — `applyOptimistic` (trims title, keeps version, records PendingOp with prev, clears banner, returns same state for unknown id), `resolveOp` (adopts server copy, drops op, same state for unknown opId), `rejectOp` (version_conflict+current → adopt current + "Conflict: …" banner; otherwise roll back to prev + error.message), and `ItemStore.edit` (unknown id → no-op; item with pending op → `"<title>" is still saving.` banner, no request; else applyOptimistic synchronously, then api.patchItem with the pre-change version, resolveOp on success / rejectOp on API error / {code:"network", message:"Network error"} on transport throw).
